findings.description: The bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so stored objects (including the seeded vendor roster) are not guaranteed to be encrypted with a managed or customer key.
No ACL is set and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so bucket/object ACLs and bucket policies could grant public access without any account-level guardrail.
No logging block is configured, so unauthorised access to the report data cannot be detected or reconstructed forensically.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy is true, so objects can be silently overwritten or destroyed with no recoverable prior version, weakening data integrity and tamper-evidence.
The ledger export bucket holds financial data but defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving objects unencrypted at rest by configuration.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, allowing ledger export objects to be overwritten or permanently deleted without recovery.
No server access logging is configured for a bucket containing financial ledger exports, so access to sensitive data is not auditable.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource protects this bucket, so a later ACL or policy change could expose ledger data publicly.
The model artifacts bucket enables versioning and logging but omits server-side encryption configuration, so artifacts are stored without enforced encryption.
No public access block is associated with the bucket, leaving no guardrail against accidental public ACLs or policies.
Operational runbooks frequently contain sensitive internal procedures and credentials references, yet the bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration.
No logging block is configured, so reads and writes to the runbooks bucket are not recorded for audit or incident response.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined, so the private ACL is the only barrier to exposure and can be overridden by a policy change.

The ACL value "lcatalogopts-delivery-write" is not a valid canned ACL (the intended value is "log-delivery-write"), so the audit/log destination bucket's access control is misconfigured and log delivery or intended permissions will not be applied as expected.

force_destroy = true on the audit trail bucket allows all audit logs to be deleted along with the bucket, undermining tamper-resistance of the audit record; no object lock or MFA delete is configured.
The bucket that aggregates access logs has no public access block, so a misapplied ACL or policy could expose audit data.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing third-party PII/contact data) is uploaded from the repository into a bucket with no default encryption and no explicit kms_key_id or server_side_encryption argument on the object.
